title: Grab and Move doesn't work through Google Chrome Remote Desktop
author: finlaybob

status.label: Remote-session input reproduction is ready
status.detail: Grab and Move fails through both Chrome Remote Desktop and Parsec while a comparable tool works, but the report does not establish whether remote clients suppress low-level hook events, alter injected flags, or expose a session/elevation boundary.

next_action.label: Trace remote modifier and mouse events
next_action.reason: Run a controlled maintainer reproduction before proposing a compatibility fix.

judgment.rationale: The two-machine steps are sufficient for reproduction and a second remote product confirms the class of failure. Current Grab and Move uses global low-level keyboard and mouse hooks, ignores injected keyboard events, and samples physical modifier state, all of which can behave differently under remote input.
evidence: Chrome Remote Desktop with Send System Keys enabled does not activate Grab and Move.
A second reporter confirms the same behavior through Parsec.
AltSnap reportedly works in the same Chrome Remote Desktop environment.
Current Grab and Move installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL and WH_MOUSE_LL hooks and ignores LLKHF_INJECTED keyboard events.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce while tracing hook delivery and flags, then decide whether compatibility can be added without accepting unsafe synthetic input.

fix_assessment.rationale: A code fix is premature until maintainers determine which event or state differs under remote input and whether accepting that input is safe.

issue_context.summary: Grab and Move fails through both Chrome Remote Desktop and Parsec while a comparable tool works, but the report does not establish whether remote clients suppress low-level hook events, alter injected flags, or expose a session/elevation boundary.
known_information: The report includes exact two-machine prerequisites, Windows build, remote-host version, and a diagnostic ZIP.
The failure affects both moving and resizing.
Local behavior is implied to work.
A comparable third-party tool works remotely.
inferences: Remote clients may mark modifier events as injected, causing Grab and Move to forward them without updating its activation state.
Remote-session key-state APIs may not match hook delivery even when system keys are forwarded.
issue_context.analysis: Because remote-input trust and event semantics are central, the safe lightweight result is a maintainer trace rather than a speculative change to injected-event filtering.
initial_investigation: Read the complete body, diagnostic reference, and Parsec confirmation.
Inspected src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp for hook installation, LLKHF_INJECTED filtering, modifier state, and GetAsyncKeyState use.
Found no linked upstream fix or assignee.

actions.label: Trace Grab and Move over remote desktop

reproduce.version_requirements: PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer; current Chrome Remote Desktop and Parsec if available
prerequisites: Use two computers and enable Grab and Move locally on the host.
Enable system-key forwarding in the remote client.
Prepare a normal non-elevated window and confirm local Alt/Win plus mouse drag works first.
steps: Connect with Chrome Remote Desktop and attempt move and resize with the configured activation modifier.
Record keyboard and mouse low-level hook delivery, injected flags, scan codes, and GetAsyncKeyState for the modifier.
Repeat through Parsec and compare with a local attempt.
Repeat with AltSnap only as a behavioral comparison, without inferring identical hook policy.
reproduce.expected_result: The trace should identify whether missing, injected, or inconsistent modifier/mouse state prevents activation; local behavior must remain correct.
